To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ising model contains two null vector levels, at which the null vectors have weights 3/2 and 5/2, while in the tricritical Ising model only one such level occurs, at weight 3/2.
the Ising model contains a null vector at level 5 and that the tricritical model does not.

the null vector at level 5 in the Ising model implies the proportionality of the tensor currents of dimension six and the vanishing (at the critical point) of four of the first five composite operators in the OPE’s of the stress‐energy tensor with the Fermi field, whereas the null vector at the same level in the supersymmetric tritritical model only implies the vanisheing of the composite fermi current of dimension 9/2.
